- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- Underestimate during sentiment dips (sentiment < 0.4) — add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >80.0) — cap forecast at +5% above peak to avoid overcorrection.
- Lagged mean reversion: if 3–5 days of downward trend in history, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent low.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment is rising (last 3 days > 0.7), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating >0.6 and <0.4), use 20d moving average of price to anchor forecast instead of 30d trend.
